title: ChIP protocol
author: Krishnaprasad G. Nandanan
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.tkyekxw
materials: 1 L RNase A was added to all the samples and incubated overnight at 65ºC in a thermo block for removing RNA and to reverse the crosslinks.
To each of the 200 µL aliquots, 7.5 L of proteinase K (20 mg/mL) was added and incubated at 50ºC for 2 h in thermo block.

For DNA isolation 1 mL Buffer PB (QIAGEN) and 10 L of 3M Sodium acetate pH 5.2 was added and incubated at 37ºC for 30 minutes. DNA purification was done using column method with Qiagen PCR Purification Kit. The two WCE which was divided to two aliquots earlier were combined at this point, and the DNA was eluted with 50 µL TE pH 8.0. Samples were stored at -20ºC until analysis by sequencing or qPCR.

steps.title: Collect yeast culture and pellet cells
steps.instruction: Harvest 50 mL of SPO medium yeast culture (≈4 × 10⁷ cells/mL) and centrifuge at 4000 RPM for 5 min. Discard supernatant.

steps.title: Lyse cells with glass beads
steps.instruction: Resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL lysis buffer, add 900 µL acid‑washed glass beads (425‑600 µm), and lyse by shaking in a Mini‑Beadbeater‑8 for 1 min × 18 cycles, keeping samples on ice for 2 min between cycles. Verify breakage efficiency with a hemocytometer.

steps.title: Clean tube tops and collect lysate
steps.instruction: Wipe the tops of the screw‑cap tubes with 70 % ethanol, puncture a small hole in each cap, and invert the tubes into a 15 mL polystyrene tube. Centrifuge at 4000 RPM for 1 min at 4 °C to collect the cell extract. Add 1 mL lysis buffer to the beads, centrifuge again to recover the complete lysate.

steps.title: Sonicate chromatin with Bioruptor
steps.instruction: Insert a 15 mL tube adaptor (metallic bar must not touch tube wall) and place tubes in a Bioruptor water tank filled with pre‑chilled Milli‑Q water and a layer of ice. Sonicate the lysate at low intensity (30 s ON / 30 s OFF) for 10 min, then replace the ice and water. Repeat this sonication cycle two more times (total three 10‑min cycles). Transfer the lysate to a 2 mL tube and centrifuge at 13 000 RPM for 5 min at 4 °C; move the supernatant to a fresh 15 mL tube. Add fresh ice and pre‑chilled water to the tank and sonicate the lysate for another 10 min; change ice and water and repeat once more (two additional 10‑min cycles).

steps.title: Assess sonication efficiency
steps.instruction: Take 10 µL of the lysate, add 190 µL TE/1 % SDS, extract DNA as described later, elute with 30 µL TE, and run half of the eluate on a 1.2 % agarose gel. An average fragment size of ~300–400 bp indicates successful sonication.

steps.title: Prepare and block Protein A beads
steps.instruction: Follow the manufacturer’s protocol to prepare Protein A sepharose beads. Use 50 µL beads per sample. Wash beads twice with 400 µL PBS/BSA, then block by incubating the beads in 400 µL PBS/BSA on a rotating wheel at 4 °C for ~4 h.

steps.title: Pre‑clear lysate with beads
steps.instruction: Wash the blocked beads twice with 1 mL lysis buffer. Keep the lysate on ice, add it to the washed beads, and rotate at 4 °C for 1 h.

steps.title: Add antibody and incubate for IP
steps.instruction: Separate the pre‑clearing beads by centrifugation at 1000 RPM for 1 min; collect the supernatant. Reserve 10 µL for Western blot and 20 µL as Input (store at –20 °C and 4 °C, respectively). Add 5 µL Msh5 antibody (2.5 µL per 1 mL aliquot) to the IP portion of the supernatant and rotate at 4 °C for 6 h. Prior to antibody addition, wash the blocked beads twice with 400 µL PBS/BSA and remove PBS/BSA by centrifugation (1000 RPM, 1 min). Then add the lysate‑antibody mixture to the beads and rotate another 6 h at 4 °C.

steps.title: Separate beads and store aliquots
steps.instruction: After the 6‑h incubation, centrifuge at 1000 RPM for 1 min. Collect 10 µL of the supernatant for Western blot (store at –20 °C). Freeze the remaining lysate in liquid nitrogen and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Wash immunoprecipitated beads
steps.instruction: Perform the following washes, rotating on a rotor for 3 min at room temperature for each wash:

substeps.instruction: Two washes with 1 mL lysis buffer.
Two washes with 1 mL lysis buffer + 360 mM NaCl.
Two washes with 1 mL washing buffer (10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8, 250 mM LiCl, 0.5 % Na‑deoxycholate, 1 mM EDTA, 0.5 % Triton X‑100).
One wash with 1 mL TE wash buffer (10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8, 1 mM EDTA, 0.5 % Triton X‑100).
During the first and last wash, suspend beads in the wash solution and transfer them to a Protein LoBind tube.

steps.title: Remove wash buffer from beads
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the beads at low speed (1000 RPM, 1 min) and discard all supernatant completely.

steps.title: Elute DNA from beads
steps.instruction: Add 40 µL elution buffer (50 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8, 10 mM EDTA, 1 % SDS) to the beads, incubate at 65 °C for 15 min with shaking, then centrifuge at 13 000 RPM for 1 s and transfer the supernatant to a new 1.5 mL tube. Add 160 µL TE/1 % SDS to the beads, vortex, centrifuge again at 13 000 RPM for 1 s, and combine this supernatant with the first eluate. Take 10 µL of the combined eluate for Western blot (store at –20 °C).

steps.title: Process input sample
steps.instruction: To the previously saved 20 µL input sample, add 380 µL TE/1 % SDS, mix, and split into two aliquots.

steps.title: Downstream DNA analysis
steps.instruction: Use the eluted DNA for Illumina HiSeq 2500 sequencing (50‑bp single‑end) and for qPCR. For qPCR, calculate percent enrichment relative to input and then compute fold enrichment versus the early 2 h time point.
